So I've finished the game in around 23 hours on commander difficulty and I have no desire to play it again whatsoever. And here's why:

The game is quite addicting in the beginning. You are eager to enhance your space station, build new stronger spaceships, train your commanders, expand your resource mining facilities and so on. But as the time goes on, it gets repetetive and tiresome and by the time you defeat your first spire, you just want to be done with the game already. So why does it feel like a chore? Well, the progress you make in this game feels unrewarding and pointless and the game itself is as shallow as that blonde chick in second grade that helped you discover what boners are. It just painfully lacks in depth. The tech tree is useless, you gather anough resources to research everything by the time you are half through the game. Spaceship skills are meaningles, you will end up using random skills while engaging in combat just to save yourself the hassle of choosing between identical differently painted skills that make almost no difference to the outcome of the fight whatsoever. The expanding part of the game is atrocious. Enemy alien rifts keep spawning aliens in your territory just to annoy you and since the combat system is so dull, you just roll your eyes everytime a new rift spawns. It's not a challenge, it's an inconvenience that really hurts the experience. And higher difficulties promise higher hitting enemies that have more HP? Talk about artificial difficulty. I found that the only truly challanging part of the game is bugs, way too many of them for my comfort. The diplomatic part of the game is virtually non-existant. Looking through the achievements I learned that I could have become allies with other species, but I highly doubt it would have gotten any effect on the gameplay. The procedural generation of the map goes to the extent of resource locations changing places with each other and alien rifts spawning in different locations. Well, What about customization, such neat 4X title should surely deliver on that front, right? I'm sure you know the answer by now. So is there anything this game has to offer that could make up for all that? I honestly don't think so. It does have beautiful pixel art, enjoyable soundtrack and decent story with little bits of humour here and there, but that's about it. It would be a much better little comic or a short animated story than a video game.

tl;dr:

PROS:
+beautiful pixel art
+enjoyable soundtrack
+decent story
+chuckle-worthy humour

CONS:
-painfully shallow
-repetitive and tiresome
-artificial difficulty
-unrewarding grind and progress
-tech tree, skill and combat systems are dull and at times entirelly pointless
-diplomatic choices don't matter
-territory expansion is very limited
-procedural generation goes to the extent of making you feel like eating the same apple but with your left hand this time
-customization non-existant
-BUGS
-the game plays itself for you while constantly annoying you at the same time

Verdict: just play FTL

The combat system for this game is great. It's turn based like some RPGs. Depending on the ship you build, your officer and the promotions you've given your officer, each ship has a different set of actions it can take that mostly boil down to attacking or healing. Each action also adds buffs or debuffs to the one performing it and/or the target. In addition to that, most actions "exploit" certain debuffs. So, when you're thinking strategically, you may have one ship do a weaker attack that creates the "crew panic" debuff so that your other ship, whose attack "exploits" crew panic is more successful. Then, the actions have warm-ups, cool downs, etc. that make them available at different stages in the battle. This also means that types of ships/officers you combine to make a fleet (science, engineering, tactical) will allow very different dynamics of play. Overall, all of this allows for a lot of strategy in combat.

The rest of the game is pretty interesting and has that star trek feel (making it more than just a battle game). You have to explore your own base (which you took from an alien race before the game starts) and build it up with systems. You have to research tecs, build ships, train officers, visit star systems to pick up resources. Exploring and running the ship involves choice events, crew demands and battles with aliens you find on the ship. Your star systems keep being harassed by enemis (part of the overarching story) so you have to protect them. There are also many mini-missions for other civilizations.

The game is halfway between real-time and turn-based in that it's real-time but pauses any time anything happens.

I do have a few complaints:

1. The interface outside of the battles is clunky. I feel like I'm constantly hopping between screens. A lot of actions and information seem somewhat buried in the interface. At times, I've used a pen and paper to keep track of some things.
2. There is a lot of arbitrary walling off of stuff. For example, most actions in the game (researching, exploring, fighting, engineering) must be done by an officer. But the same exact action (ex: exploring a room, training a new officer) will require a level up to do again. So, the game feels like a lot of waiting to level up so that I can do the thing I want to do next.
3. Resource gathering feels like a chore. Ideally, I'd just have a low rank officer use a previous generation ship to shuttle around picking up resources, but that involves micromanaging to tell them each move to do and since it's real-time, it's a lot of juggling back and forth. Being able to delegate to an officer to repeat such a simple task should be built in. Instead, to automate this micromanagement task, you have to have a level 4 officer crank away making drones and fly a level 4 officer to each planet to install those drones. Both of these actions take a long time and, given the shortage of officers mentioned above, it shuts you out from a lot of actions to have to block out one or two officers like this.

Overall, it's an addictive game and is fun to play. I'm still on my first playthrough so maybe I'll learn better ways to do some of these things.

总体评价:性价比很高的一款游戏, 星际策略类游戏这个类型是我最近尝试的. 躺愿望清单里几次都没舍得扔, 最后趁今年年末有时间通关大捷. 分别从以下几方面说一说:

1. 游戏画面: 典型的像素风, 后一个版本中的光速指挥官中的像更加具有美感, 个人比较喜欢这中风格,所以在我比较讨喜啦. 而且在不同飞船状态的下的受伤情况都有仔去画. 宇宙背景的色调也没有被像素的画质影响, 依然能够感受深广袤的宇宙, 身临其境.不错

2. 游戏战斗: 回合战斗, 主分为分为陆地站和空间站, 简单点说就是人和怪兽打, 飞船和怪兽打. 设计人员将角色分为工程师, 科学家决策师每种都有不同的技能特色, 可以相互配合. 这里介绍的是可以相互引爆, 比如飞船对对面上了一个混乱的Buff, 那么你的同伴利用引爆这个Buff获得更高的伤害. 也是在编队和设置技能时候需要考量策略一个点关不同星球各自状态,不同地点因为磁场或者酸雨缘故有些Buff是上不了的. 配合上战斗的音乐打也不怎么枯燥, 但怪物的类型有些单一.

3. 游戏音乐: 8bit风格音乐搭配不同的能焕然一新的感觉. 狡黠的外星人音乐也会做出让人捉摸不透的音调, 战斗中音乐紧张和略带压迫的星际感, 探索未知星球的迷离都把握的比较好. 喜欢的朋友完全可音轨.

4. 游戏剧情: 主线突出,支线刚好.作为一个20多个小时绝对能通关的游戏, 主线做到清晰的指引情况下, 能够编辑出3条左右的旁线再加上一些外星文明的对话来调剂. 在剧情这方面我能说对的起这20几块钱了. 不可能也不应该一款轻量级策略游戏要求像神界2 那样把文本量做的和小说一样. 所刚刚好.


总体来说还是不错的, 但是新的版本对于人物角色的培养有点整的复杂的样子, 不过制作人想突出角色培养的概念还是值得肯定的.如果非要希望加点儿什么或者有什么改进的话, 我个人希望把行船建设和人物培养做的更加有趣一点也突一些陆地战的用途, 因为原作里面感觉陆地战好像没什么用,有点儿鸡肋.

还没有尝试过策略太空回合制像素风游戏的玩家,这款Halcyon6 非常值得你入手.
